propositions: The T11 post-rollback schema state paragraph generates near-identical tautological findings that are meaningless against an append-only store and drown rare real catches.

Post-rollback-state findings should be raised only under four conditions: reinterpreting persisted records, in-place record rewrite/migration, removing or narrowing a read path, or a one-way transformation with no back-out.
An anti-false-positive line must exempt purely additive, backward-compatible persistence changes (new record/event types, optional fields, new tables/columns with defaults).
The applicability rule must be portable and name no store technology so it applies to SQL migrations, event stores, document databases, and config formats.
A per-plan finding cap was rejected in favor of an applicability rule that removes the tautology class at its source; posture remains advisory.
Rubric contract tests must assert the four conditions and anti-FP line are present and the old unconditional wording is gone.
